clue.text: Leo possibly seeing good chieftains travelling around end of Suez

indicators.note: things that are travelling move about, so these letters move into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one letter is kept
to go around something is to enclose it, so the shuffled letters wrap round another piece

blocks.note: both words taken as written, to be shuffled together

explanation.surface: A man called Leo watches good tribal leaders journeying round the far end of the Suez Canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' looks like a single G but is used whole as part of the fodder; the Z from Suez is slipped in between THE and ODIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve astrological star signs, and 'possibly' marks it as just one example of them.

clue.text: Spartan's strides to falter and flag

indicators.note: to falter is to stumble unsteadily, so the letters lose their footing and fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A tough Spartan soldier's marching steps begin to stumble and he tires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a verb meaning tire, paired with 'falter', but it is the noun naming the definition; the possessive S counts in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the popular name of the national banner of the United States.

clue.text: Reach old woman in boat returning

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
returning means going back the way it came, so the whole thing is read backwards

blocks.note: MA is an informal word for mother, a familiar 'old woman'
a tug is a small boat that tows ships

explanation.surface: Reach your elderly mother as she sits in a boat heading back to shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach' looks like an instruction to get to her, but it is a noun meaning range. The container is built first and only then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the full range or scope of something, just as one's reach is the extent of what can be covered.

clue.text: Shock from power failure around end of October

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so just that letter is kept
to be around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: an outage is a cut in the electricity supply

explanation.surface: People are shocked by a blackout at the end of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power failure' gives a chiefly American word for a power cut, which is then split open to take one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong feeling of shocked anger, so the two nouns share the sense of indignant surprise.

clue.text: Knitter modified knick-knack

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who knits has altered a small ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is fodder, indicator and definition with nothing else, a compact quiptic anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a small ornament of little value, which is exactly what a knick-knack is.

clue.text: Young flyers, say, holding adult licences

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' means
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Junior pilots, for example, hold grown-up flying licences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young flyers' suggests trainee pilots but means baby birds; 'say' standing for 'for example' is a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaglets are the chicks of eagles, so they are birds that will fly but are still immature.

clue.text: In theory working daily

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: In principle, someone works every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adverb but is a noun for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in written plans or calculations, not necessarily in practice, which is what theoretically means.

clue.text: Bring in worker for chief

blocks.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
a worker ant is the commonest kind

explanation.surface: Hire a new member of staff to be the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chief' reads as a noun for the boss, but it is the adjective meaning main; 'worker' for ANT is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief concern is a principal one, and important things are of the greatest significance.

clue.text: Well done ragout contains head of lettuce chopped up

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken
chopped-up food is cut into bits and mixed, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A thoroughly cooked stew includes some shredded lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' reads as how the ragout is cooked, and 'contains' looks like a container signal, but it is just fodder letters.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Well done!' and 'Congratulations!' are both exclamations of praise for an achievement.

clue.text: Owning commercial US college can gratify leader

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the word's first letter is the one kept

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial on TV or radio

explanation.surface: An American college that owns a TV advertisement can please its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess it, and admitting a fault is the same act of confession.

clue.text: Quickly visit Post Office to get code for debit card

explanation.surface: Nip into the post office for a new card PIN.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads almost literally, which is the disguise: the errand is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop in is to call somewhere briefly and casually, a short informal visit.

clue.text: Group support for an unfortunate event

blocks.note: a set is a group of things
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A support group for people who have suffered a misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group support' reads as a single counselling phrase, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal of progress, a piece of bad luck that holds someone back.

clue.text: Agent and setter returning alternative ruler

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
the crossword setter refers to themselves as ME

explanation.surface: A secret agent and a setter come back with a different leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Only REP and ME turn round; OR is added afterwards. 'Setter' for ME is a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, so he is a supreme monarch who governs.

clue.text: Consume repasts regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other one, so alternate letters are kept

explanation.surface: Have your meals at regular times.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters are taken, not the odd ones, which would give RPSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to swallow it as nourishment, the everyday act of eating.

clue.text: A fellow repeatedly found in home is most uncool

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: F abbreviates fellow, and it appears twice
a nest is a home, often used figuratively

explanation.surface: A man who keeps turning up at your house is deeply unfashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF is British slang for tacky or unstylish; F for fellow is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff means lacking style or taste, so the superlative describes whatever is least trendy of all.

clue.text: Dash around after blonde European, thus giving producers a proper deal

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun: fair trade is the practice that does this

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards
coming after something means placed behind it, fixing the running order

explanation.surface: Rushing about after a fair-haired European, so farmers get a decent price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash around' sounds like rushing about, but 'around' turns the word for dash back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair trade is a scheme ensuring growers in poorer countries receive equitable prices for their goods.

clue.text: Heads of South Korean institute go downhill fast

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The leaders of a Korean institution are in rapid decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go downhill fast' sounds like decline or failure, but it is literal: sliding down a snowy slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to glide down snowy mountain slopes on long runners, often at speed.

clue.text: Employee in rowdy taverns

indicators.note: a rowdy crowd is disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A worker employed in noisy pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like placing the employee inside the pubs, but it only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is a person hired to perform duties for another, which is a kind of worker on staff.

clue.text: Oddly envies the first lady

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept

explanation.surface: Strangely, she is jealous of the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first lady' suggests the US President's spouse, but it means the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Eve was the earliest woman created, so she is literally the original lady.

clue.text: Celebration of son getting back ending finally after one

indicators.note: finally means at the very end, so the word's last letter is kept
placed after something means put behind it, fixing which piece comes second

blocks.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: A party for a son who has returned, the ending finally coming after a single event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' reads as returning, but 'back' gives HIND on its own; G comes after I.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or festive gathering.

clue.text: Film following flyer sent up and left to drop

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top
following means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end

explanation.surface: A film about a bird that was launched skyward and left to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning a small droplet.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a tiny amount of liquid, a small trickle or droplet.

clue.text: Great secretary is a relative

explanation.surface: An excellent secretary turns out to be a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' looks like part of a family term such as great-uncle, but it gives GRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandpa is a grandfather, a parent's father and so a family member by blood.

clue.text: Revolting jerk taking part in genuine performance

indicators.note: revolting can mean turning over, so the word is flipped round
to take part in something is to be inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tic is a sudden involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A disgusting idiot is appearing in an authentic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting jerk' reads as an insult, but 'Revolting' means turning over and 'jerk' is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert or reading given by a performer, so it is a kind of show.

clue.text: Controls regarding home trespass

blocks.note: being in means being at home
trespass is an old word for sin, as in the Lord's Prayer

explanation.surface: Rules concerning entering someone's property without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Controls' looks like a plural noun but is a verb; 'trespass' means sin, not entering land.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse is to pull it back with the straps, so figuratively it means to restrain.

clue.text: The French overwhelmed by roach-spread disease

indicators.note: something spread is scattered about, so the letters are scattered into a new order
to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed, so one piece is swallowed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be shuffled

explanation.surface: The French were overcome by an illness carried by cockroaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roach-spread' reads as one compound adjective, but the hyphen hides a word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute bacterial infection of the intestine, spread through contaminated water.

clue.text: Eggs in line for auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so the word is as heard rather than as spelt

explanation.surface: Eggs laid in a row for an accountant checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it just means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs inside a female fish, eaten as food.

clue.text: Drink sprayed initially in part of eye

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
something in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye

explanation.surface: A drink splashed into someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' could be a verb, but it is a noun naming a Greek wine flavoured with pine resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a resinated white wine from Greece, an alcoholic beverage served chilled.

clue.text: Section of choir on outing showing resolve

indicators.note: a section is one part of a whole, so the letters are a run inside the following words

blocks.note: the run spans the end of choir, all of on and the start of outing

explanation.surface: Part of the choir on a trip displays determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' suggests a choir section such as altos; 'resolve' looks like a noun for determination but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out problems is to settle or smooth them away, which is what resolving difficulties means.

clue.text: Old Ford carrying it into city

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, SA
the Ka is a small Ford car model

explanation.surface: An old Ford car carries it into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal is a crossword convention; the Ford Ka was a small hatchback sold in Europe, not the old Model T the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port and the third-largest urban area in Japan.

clue.text: Fruit left for gem of a girl

explanation.surface: Fruit left out for a lovely girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gem of a girl' sounds like praise, but it asks for a girl's name that is also a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is both a precious gem found in oysters and a female first name.

clue.text: Outlaw party involving especially long time with Duke

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A banned party that lasts a particularly long time and includes a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a verb meaning ban, describing the party, but it is the noun defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, especially in the old American West.

clue.text: Dame's new fantasy sadly amounts to nothing

indicators.note: things that turn out sadly have gone wrong, so the letters go wrong and come out in a different order

blocks.note: all three words taken as written, including the possessive S

explanation.surface: An elderly lady's latest daydream comes to nothing, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; the signal is 'sadly'. Sweet Fanny Adams is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, often shortened to sweet FA, is a British slang expression meaning absolutely zero.
